strategies.name: Fused Local Operations Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Merge all local permutation, scaling, and division operations into single vectorized kernels between each all_reduce, reducing the number of separate tensor operations from ~4W operations per iteration to 1-2 per iteration. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but dramatically fewer local kernel launches. Trades code complexity for reduced host-device synchronization overhead.

strategies.name: Precompute Permutation and Scale Masks
strategies.desc: Precompute all permutation indices and scaling factors (a[r], 1/a[r], a[r]/W) as static tensors before the loop, then use gather/scatter or advanced indexing for O(1) local operations. 8 all_reduce dispatches with highly optimized local ops. Trades memory (storing W×S index/scale tensors) for faster repeated local operations.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Concatenation
strategies.desc: Stack multiple iterations' worth of buffers along a batch dimension, issue fewer but larger all_reduce operations (e.g., 2-4 dispatches instead of 8 by batching pairs/quads of iterations). Requires careful dependency analysis since iterations are dependent, but independent sub-computations within each iteration can be batched. Fewer dispatches but larger payload per dispatch.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter and All-Gather
strategies.desc:
Decompose each all_reduce into reduce_scatter + all_gather phases, overlapping computation and communication by starting the next iteration's local ops while previous iteration's all_gather completes. 16 collective dispatches (8×2) but with potential overlap hiding latency. Represents communication-computation pipelining tradeoff.
